protections: P1 (present, fetch only): fetchTask rejects any argument matching /^--upload-pack(=|$)/ before the command runs (simple-git/src/lib/tasks/fetch.ts:7, simple-git/src/lib/tasks/fetch.ts:17); this is the only transport-safety guard in the pinned tree and it is recorded as the earlier security release (simple-git/CHANGELOG.md:13).

P2 (absent): no command refuses an ext:: remote URL; clone, mirror, fetch, pull, push, submodule-add, remote-add, ls-remote and raw all place caller strings straight into git's argv (simple-git/src/lib/tasks/clone.ts:24, simple-git/src/lib/tasks/fetch.ts:12, simple-git/src/lib/tasks/pull.ts:8, simple-git/src/lib/tasks/push.ts:14, simple-git/src/lib/tasks/sub-module.ts:5, simple-git/src/lib/tasks/remote.ts:6, simple-git/src/git.js:368).

P3 (absent): program-selection options other than fetch's literal --upload-pack are never rejected; clone and pull accept --upload-pack through the shared option expansion (simple-git/src/lib/utils/task-options.ts:15, simple-git/src/lib/tasks/clone.ts:24) and push accepts --receive-pack through the same path (simple-git/src/lib/tasks/push.ts:14).

P4 (absent): transport URLs that are stored rather than passed in argv are not covered by any guard - a remote URL written into .git/config by addRemote, or a submodule URL taken from .gitmodules, reaches git without appearing in the command line (simple-git/src/lib/tasks/remote.ts:5, simple-git/src/lib/tasks/sub-module.ts:21, simple-git/src/lib/tasks/fetch.ts:13).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: mirror is documented as clone with --mirror, so a clone-side guard is assumed to cover it
fetch already rejects unsafe arguments, so this path reads as already guarded and the ext:: shape is not re-examined
pull is fetch plus merge, so the fetch-side rejection is assumed to cover the same arguments
push only sends objects, so it is not treated as part of the clone/fetch attack surface
git already restricts submodule URLs, so the repo argument of submodule add is assumed safe
remote add only writes configuration, so nothing is executed at the moment the URL is supplied
raw is the documented escape hatch; its arguments are the caller's responsibility
ls-remote only lists refs and downloads no objects, so it is treated as read-only
the URL lives in the repository's git config and never passes through this API, so the library is assumed not to own this check
the URLs come from the cloned repository's .gitmodules, not from any argument this library receives
the published fix was about --upload-pack in fetch, so the option is believed to be handled already
receive-pack names a program on the remote side, so the client is assumed to be safe
a broad rule that refuses any argument containing ext:: looks harmless because ext:: rarely appears in commit messages or search terms

conflicts.what: Blocking every argv element that contains ext:: closes clone/fetch/pull/push but also refuses legitimate commit messages and grep terms that mention ext:: (simple-git/src/lib/tasks/commit.ts:8, simple-git/src/lib/tasks/grep.ts:92); the rule must be scoped to transport positions.

Pinning -c protocol.ext.allow=never on every spawn closes stored-URL ext:: routes but overrides an application's deliberate protocol.ext.allow=always supplied through the supported config option (simple-git/src/lib/git-factory.ts:52, simple-git/src/lib/plugins/command-config-prefixing-plugin.ts:10), so an explicit override path is required.

Generalising the fetch rejection into a shared plugin changes it from a configurationErrorTask (simple-git/src/lib/tasks/fetch.ts:18, simple-git/src/lib/tasks/task.ts:22) to a plugin exception raised inside attemptTask (simple-git/src/lib/runners/git-executor-chain.ts:64), a contract asserted by existing tests (simple-git/test/unit/fetch.spec.ts:65).

fairness_risks: A rule keyed on the literal substring ext:: refuses commit messages, grep patterns and file paths that contain it (simple-git/src/lib/tasks/commit.ts:8, simple-git/src/lib/tasks/grep.ts:92, simple-git/src/git.js:368).

A hard ext:: block contradicts deliberate use of the ext transport through the supported config option (simple-git/src/lib/utils/simple-git-options.ts:6, simple-git/src/lib/git-factory.ts:52); the pinned options type has no override field (simple-git/src/lib/types/index.ts:115).
Banning --upload-pack outright, as fetch.ts:7-9 does, also refuses a custom upload-pack program on the user's own remote; no opt-in exists at the pin.

Moving the fetch rejection to a shared plugin changes the error class and the moment of rejection (simple-git/src/lib/tasks/task.ts:22 vs simple-git/src/lib/runners/git-executor-chain.ts:64), which callers and tests rely on (simple-git/test/unit/fetch.spec.ts:65).

design.why: T1 is the surface any report points at, so it is the compulsory easy anchor that any acceptable fix automatically covers. The discriminating entries are T3 (fetch already looks guarded, but the existing check matches only --upload-pack and an ext:: URL passes, fetch.ts:7-20), T12 (the same program-selection option class at clone/pull, far from the site the earlier fix touched, fetch.ts vs clone.ts:24), T10 (an ext:: URL stored in git config so no argv check ever sees it, fetch.ts:13), and T14 (the over-block constraint: commit messages and grep terms legitimately contain ext::, commit.ts:8, grep.ts:92). This beats a clone-only or clone+pull design because every argv-visible route converges on the single spawn.args hook (simple-git/src/lib/runners/git-executor-chain.ts:82, registrations at simple-git/src/lib/git-factory.ts:56), so clone+pull+push is one guard with three symptoms; the selected set needs four separate decisions: the ext argv guard, the pack-option guard (a token class that protocol pinning cannot close), protocol pinning or URL resolution for stored URLs, and a scope/override design that keeps legitimate ext:: text working. If a reviewer treats one plugin carrying both token rules as a single guard, the design falls to three groups (ext/pack argv, stored URLs, over-block constraint), still the minimum for a stacked task.

unverified: The a_fix hash 2040de601c89 could not be resolved here (git commands are unavailable); the only prior security guard in the pinned tree is the fetch --upload-pack check described in simple-git/CHANGELOG.md:13, and the history answer assumes the two are the same fix.

Git's own protocol policy for ext:: (protocol.ext.allow / GIT_PROTOCOL_FROM_USER) was not executed, so whether a config-stored remote URL (T10) or a .gitmodules URL (T11) runs the ext helper under default settings is unconfirmed.
Whether git push --receive-pack yields client-side execution comparable to the fetch --upload-pack vector (T13) was not verified.
Whether git submodule update or clone --recurse-submodules refuses ext:: URLs taken from .gitmodules (T11) was not verified against a real git binary.

The exact shape of the later upstream fix (774648049eb3) is inferred from the plugin architecture at the pin (simple-git/src/lib/runners/git-executor-chain.ts:82, simple-git/src/lib/git-factory.ts:56-62); that commit is not in the tree, so the per-route mapping of the upstream fix is unknown.
Whether the hidden tests exercise the stored-URL and over-block routes (T10, T14), as opposed to only clone/fetch ext:: and the two opt-ins, is unknown.
